issues.description: Field 'lectureName' type differs between the exercise specification/template and the provided solution. The problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String (problem_statement.md, lines 16-18 and UML lines 63-68). The template Lecture.java leaves a TODO to add this attribute as a String (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 4). The solution declares the field as type LectureName (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 6) and also provides a separate LectureName.java class (src/de/tum/cit/ase/LectureName.java, lines 3-8). This mismatch (String vs. LectureName) creates confusion about the expected attribute type and the required API for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the lectureName representation consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) change the solution to use a plain String for the lectureName field, constructor parameter, and any getters/setters to match the UML/problem statement; or (B) update the problem statement and template to explicitly require and document the LectureName type (add LectureName.java to the template and update the UML/type annotations). Prefer option A (String) for this simple exercise unless the instructor intends to teach a value object.

issues.description: The constructor parameter list in the solution does not match the constructor signature expected by the problem statement/UML. The exercise requires a constructor initializing lectureName (String) first, then the int fields in the UML order (problem_statement.md lines 19-21). The template contains a TODO to add such a constructor (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 6). The solution's constructor uses LectureName as the first parameter type instead of String (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, signature at line 13), causing a mismatch in the expected parameter types and order.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution constructor parameters with the UML/problem statement. Either: (A) change the solution constructor to accept (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) in that order; or (B) if LectureName is intended, update the problem statement and template to require LectureName and document the constructor signature accordingly.

issues.description: The solution has an internal type/signature inconsistency: the field 'lectureName' is declared as LectureName (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 6) but the getter and setter in the same solution class use String in their signatures (getLectureName(): String at src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 22; setLectureName(String) at src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 26). This causes a compilation error in the solution and prevents students from using the provided solution code as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the solution so types are consistent and the code compiles. Options: (A) change the lectureName field to type String and keep getLectureName()/setLectureName(String); (B) change the getter/setter signatures to use LectureName (getLectureName(): LectureName, setLectureName(LectureName)) and ensure all uses are updated accordingly. Ensure the constructor and toString()/other callers are updated to match the chosen representation.
